## Lecture Twenty-One ### $MA(q)$ models $$y_t = \mu + \varepsilon_t + \theta_1 \varepsilon_{t-1} + \dots + \theta_q \varepsilon_{t-q}, \quad t = \dots, -3, -2, -1, 0, \dots$$ $\{\varepsilon_t\} \overset{i.i.d.}{\sim} N(0, \sigma^2)$ $q = 1$: $$y_t = \mu + \varepsilon_t + \theta_1 \varepsilon_{t-1} \leftarrow \text{Slutzky 1937 Summation of Random Causes}$$ $$\begin{aligned} \theta_1 = 0 &\to y_t \overset{i.i.d.}{\sim} N(\mu, \sigma^2) \\ \theta_1 > 0 &\to \text{positive correlation between } y_t \text{ \& } y_{t+1} \\ \theta_1 < 0 &\to \text{negative correlation between } y_t \text{ \& } y_{t+1} \end{aligned}$$ $$\operatorname{Corr}(y_t, y_{t+1}) = \frac{\theta_1}{1 + \theta_1^2}$$ $$\operatorname{Corr}(y_t, y_{t+h}) = 0 \quad \text{for } h \ge 2$$ --- | **Sample ACF** | **Theoretical ACF for a stationary Time Series Model** | | :--- | :--- | | $y_1, \dots, y_n$
$\text{Sample ACF}(h) =$ Sample correlation between $y_t$ & $y_{t+h}$
$= \begin{pmatrix} (y_1, y_{1+h}) \\ (y_2, y_{2+h}) \\ \vdots \\ (y_{n-h}, y_n) \end{pmatrix}$ | $\rho(h) = \operatorname{Corr}(y_t, y_{t+h})$

\bar{y})(y_{t+h} - \bar{y})}{\sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^n (y_t - \bar{y})^2 \sum_{t=1}^n (y_t - \bar{y})^2}}$$ $$= \frac{\sum_{t=1}^{n-h} (y_t - \bar{y})(y_{t+h} - \bar{y})}{\sum_{t=1}^n (y_t - \bar{y})^2} = \hat{\rho}(h) \longrightarrow \text{Calculated from Data}$$ --- Stationary Model: $\rho(h)$ : ACF of the model **$MA(1)$ model:** $y_t = \mu + \varepsilon_t + \theta \varepsilon_{t-1}$ $$\rho(h) = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if } h = 0 \\ \frac{\theta}{1 + \theta^2} & \text{if } |h| = 1 \\ 0 & \text{if } |h| \ge 2 \end{cases}$$ $\to$ looks like $MA(1)$ **$MA(q)$ model:** $y_t = \mu + \varepsilon_t + \theta_1 \varepsilon_{t-1} + \dots + \theta_q \varepsilon_{t-q}$ $\downarrow$ **ALWAYS CAUSAL & STATIONARY** $$\to \rho(h) = \begin{cases} \text{something} & \text{if } |h| \le q \\ 0 & \text{if } |h| > q \end{cases}$$ --- ### **$MA(1)$** vs **$AR(1)$** $$y_t = \mu + \varepsilon_t + \theta \varepsilon_{t-1}$$ **ALWAYS STATIONARY** $$y_t - \phi_1 y_{t-1} = \phi_0 + \varepsilon_t$$ **NOT NECESSARILY CAUSAL STATIONARY** --- **Parameter Estimation:** $\phi_0, \phi_1, \sigma$ $y = (y_t)$ $X = [1, y_{t-1}]$ `sm.OLS(y, X).fit()` **Likelihood:** $(y_1, \dots, y_n) \sim N\left(\begin{pmatrix} \mu \\ \vdots \\ \mu \end{pmatrix}, \begin{bmatrix} \ddots \end{bmatrix}\right)$ $$\operatorname{var}(y_t) = \operatorname{var}(\mu + \varepsilon_t + \theta \varepsilon_{t-1}) = \sigma^2 (1 + \theta^2)$$ $$\operatorname{Cov}(y_t, y_{t+1}) = \theta \sigma^2$$ $$\Sigma = \begin{bmatrix} \sigma^2(1+\theta^2) & \theta \sigma^2 & 0 & \dots & 0 \\ \theta \sigma^2 & \sigma^2(1+\theta^2) & \theta \sigma^2 & 0 \dots & 0 \\ 0 & \theta \sigma^2 & \sigma^2(1+\theta^2) & \theta \sigma^2 0 \dots 0 \\ & \ddots & \ddots & \ddots & \\ 0 & \dots & 0 & \theta \sigma^2 & \sigma^2(1+\theta^2) \end{bmatrix}$$ $$\frac{1}{(\sqrt{2\pi})^n \sqrt{\det \Sigma}} \exp\left[-\frac{1}{2} (y - \mu)^T \Sigma^{-1} (y - \mu)\right]$$ $$y = \begin{pmatrix} y_1 \\ \vdots \\ y_n \end{pmatrix}, \quad \mu = \begin{pmatrix} \mu \\ \vdots \\ \mu \end{pmatrix}$$ **ARIMA** $\to$ function in `statsmodels` --- **AR model:** $y_t - \phi_1 y_{t-1} - \dots - \phi_p y_{t-p} = \phi_0 + \varepsilon_t$ **MA:** $y_t = \mu + \varepsilon_t + \theta_1 \varepsilon_{t-1} + \theta_2 \varepsilon_{t-2} + \dots + \theta_q \varepsilon_{t-q}$ **ARMA($p, q$):** $$y_t - \phi_1 y_{t-1} - \dots - \phi_p y_{t-p} = \phi_0 + \varepsilon_t + \theta_1 \varepsilon_{t-1} + \dots + \theta_q \varepsilon_{t-q}$$ **ARIMA($p, d, q$):** $\downarrow$ differencing Take data $y_t$, difference $d$ times & then use $ARMA(p, q)$ `arima(data, order = (p, d, q))` $MA(q)$: `arima(data, order = (0, 0, q))` $MA(q)$ to $y_t -
